additionalCoursework: We have no recommended course of study beyond our premed course requirements. However, we encourage applicants to progress beyond the elementary level in the field of their choice rather than pursue an undirected, generalized program. The student of medicine enters a profession closely allied to the natural sciences and must be prepared to cope with chemistry and biology at the graduate level. But science courses should not be your sole focus: a liberal education is the supporting structure for graduate study and should include an understanding of the humanities, arts, and society as well as the foundations of technology and civilization.  Biostatistics is recommended (not required) beginning in the 2026-27 application year.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
Diversity is vitally important in Yale's collaborative learning environment, and applications are encouraged from individuals from groups underrepresented in medicine. The Office of Collaborative Excellence strives to create an inclusive community for the diverse student body of Yale School of Medicine by supporting and celebrating differences. Through outreach, education, and advocacy, OCE promotes the creation of an interdisciplinary healthcare workforce – including innovative physicians, researchers, and scientists – who reflect and serve the diversity of the community.

Additionally, the Office for Women in Medicine serves to promote and support the academic growth of women students, trainees, fellows and faculty in medicine and medical science across all sectors at the School of Medicine.

Information about these important offices and specific diversity groups can be found online:
https://medicine.yale.edu/excellence/
https://medicine.yale.edu/owm/
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students are expected to follow a continuous course of study at the School of Medicine. However, a student who wishes or needs to interrupt his or her study temporarily may request a leave of absence.  There are three types of leave that will be considered:  personal (because of personal exigencies), medical (because of illness or injury), and parental (for reasons of pregnancy, maternity care, or paternity care).  All leaves of absence must be approved by the Associate Dean for Student Affairs.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Student Interest Groups (SIGs) are organized around general professional areas or medical specialties, such as the Global Health SIG, Surgical SIG, Pediatrics SIG, Infectious Diseases SIG, and others. Community service organizations include an Anatomy Teaching Program for local high school students, homeless shelters, food pantries, a student-run HAVEN free clinic, and others. Social, political, literary, cultural, and religious organizations are important for many medical students. Music groups include the Medical School Symphony Orchestra, a chamber music group, a rock band, and a cappella singing groups. Intramural sports among Yale schools include soccer, basketball, softball, rugby, ice hockey, squash, flag football, and others. Elected officers of the Medical Student Council (MSC) and the Committee Overseeing Volunteer Services (COVS) play leadership roles in connection with student organizations and activities. All student groups are supported by the Office of Student Affairs.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Yale School of Medicine is in New Haven, Connecticut, a few blocks from the heart of the Yale University campus. Medical students benefit from academic and extracurricular opportunities provided by the twelve other graduate and professional schools and by the city of New Haven, a culturally diverse city located 75 miles east of New York.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Yale University housing is available for single and married students. In addition, the Office of Graduate Housing provides assistance in locating off-campus apartments near the School of Medicine and in a variety of New Haven neighborhoods.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
The Dean’s Advisory Council on Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer and Intersex Affairs collaborates with other groups to cultivate visible supports and a vibrant, connected community of LGBTQI+ individuals and their allies at YSM. The Advisory Council helps guide the expansion of LGBTQI+ health research, and coordinates efforts to foster an inclusive, patient-centered environment in which tailored care is available for LGBTQI+ patients. Furthermore, the Advisory Council oversees initiatives that prepare our trainees to serve all of their patients with excellence, regardless of sexual orientation or gender identity.

Information about this important resource can be found online:
https://medicine.yale.edu/lgbtqi/
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities:
The Office of Student Accessibility Services is committed to promoting equitable access to education and student life for students with disabilities, and to fostering a campus environment of belonging, inclusion, and respect.

Information about this important resource can be found online:
https://sas.yale.edu/
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Yale School of Medicine (YSM) and the Physician Associate Program foster a holistic approach to student well-being and promote wellness, in all its forms. We believe everyone benefits when every student feels part of the community and wants to be engaged, in whatever capacity is fulfilling to that individual. Yale University and the Yale School of Medicine have people, programs, and processes dedicated to ensuring students have the support needed to enhance access, success, and well-being.

Information about these resources can be found online: 
https://medicine.yale.edu/md-program/student-affairs/student-well-being/
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The Yale System of Medical Education has been an important part of life at the Yale School of Medicine since the 1920s. The fundamental element of the system is the concept that medical students are mature individuals, strongly motivated to learn, requiring guidance and stimulation rather than compulsion or competition for relative standing in a group. The corollary of this concept is that students must assume more than usual responsibility for their education. Students should be considered adults in a graduate school and be permitted to enjoy as large a degree of freedom as is consistent with the fulfillment of requirements for the degree of Doctor of Medicine. Memorization of facts should be far less important than a well-rounded education in fundamental principles, training in methods of investigation, and the acquisition of the scientific habit of mind.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: While it is not necessary to bring a car, our students find it is more convenient to have a car. Advantages include more flexible commute to clinical rotations and ease to do errands and groceries. If you already own a car, it may be helpful to bring it. Our Yale System fosters a warm and collaborative environment, so students without cars are able to carpool with other students who are on the same rotation!

medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Interaction with patients begins almost immediately after matriculation in the first year.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Instruction takes place in lectures, small study groups, and laboratory sessions.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations begin in January of the second year and take place over two semesters at Yale New Haven Hospital and other affiliated hospitals.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: Summer to Advance Research Training @ Yale is an optional 8-week prematriculation program where ~15 students with a keen interest in medical research conduct research projects under faculty guidance.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance policy varies according to the specific course.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: Our curriculum, launched in 2015, embraces the proud traditions of our past while keeping an eye towards the future. Nine Competencies and Five Guiding Principles form the foundation of the curriculum. You will see that these goals focus on areas essential for students to become successful future leaders in medicine. In addition, our Guiding Principles ensure that the curriculum is built upon the principles and values of the Yale system of medical education, including respect for student initiative and maturity, curricular flexibility, close faculty mentoring and a required thesis to promote scientific inquiry, all hallmarks of our unique learning environment.  Information about Competencies and Guiding Principles can be found here: https://medicine.yale.edu/md-program/curriculum/
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Through the Interprofessional Longitudinal Clinical Experience (ILCE) program, first-year students are directly involved in patient care from the beginning of medical school, with an emphasis on interprofessional education, team-based care, attention to the patient experience, and building clinical skills. Following the ILCE, medical students work in small groups in the Medical Coaching Experience (MCE) with physician mentors to refine their clinical skills with patients. During the clerkship year, the 12-week primary care and mental health clerkship provides intensive experience in primary care, including opportunities in family medicine, internal medicine, psychiatry, and pediatrics. Students work closely with community physicians and patients in office-based practices. All of these experiences are required. In addition, Yale sponsors a student-run free clinic in New Haven, another important primary care site at which students volunteer throughout medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: The School of Medicine supports clinical research and basic science research for MD and MD/PhD students in a wide variety of fields and settings. Of special note, Yale medical students have been required since 1839 to complete a thesis based on original research. Fellowships, including the Downs Fellowship, Doris Duke Fellowships, and Howard Hughes Medical Institute Fellowships, are administered by the Office of Student Research.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: For 3 semesters, the Basic & Clinical Science Curriculum includes 8 Master Courses, 4 Longitudinal Courses, and 9 Longitudinal Threads. Integrated Clinical Clerkships begin in January of the 2nd year.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Though not required, community service is extremely important for Yale students.  Opportunities for community service are available in New Haven, elsewhere in the region, and internationally.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: A thesis based on original research has been required of all Yale medical students since 1839.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Yale New Haven Health System includes Yale New Haven Hospital, Smilow Cancer Hospital, Bridgeport and Greenwich Hospitals, and other major hospitals in Connecticut, Rhode Island, and New York State.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Pass/fail for preclinical courses and clerkships. Four-tier grading system for clinical sub-internships and four week electives.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Yale School of Medicine was established in 1810 as the Medical Institution of Yale College. The present-day Yale-New Haven Medical Center includes the School of Medicine, the School of Public Health, the School of Nursing, the Physician Associate Program, Yale-New Haven Hospital, and Smilow Cancer Hospital.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: Yale School of Medicine educates and nurtures creative leaders in medicine and science, promoting curiosity and critical inquiry in an inclusive environment enriched by diversity. We advance discovery and innovation fostered by partnerships across the University, our local community, and the world. We care for patients with compassion, and commit to improving the health of all people.

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: Criminal Background Checks are conducted after authorization by AMCAS, and results are sent to the School of Medicine. There is no charge to students for this service.
medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Accepted applicants must respond by April 30. Accepts off the waitlist before June 1 must respond within 5 business days and accepts after June 1 must respond within 2 business days.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
After the application has been submitted, additional letters of recommendation can be submitted through the AMCAS letter service. Such letters will be included with the application and will be considered by the admissions committee.

It is important that the letters provide information and support that will be informative and helpful to the Admissions Committee, supplementing the information that appears elsewhere in your application.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
A Premedical Committee letter is recommended for all MD and MD/PhD candidates. If your school does not have a Premedical Committee, you may submit at least three individual letters of recommendation. These letters should come from individuals who are in a position to comment knowledgeably on your accomplishments, abilities, experience, and/or personal qualifications. They may come from those who have taught you or worked with you in undergraduate or graduate school classes, in research settings, clinical settings, extracurricular or community service activities, professional settings, or other contexts. It is helpful to have at least one of the letters from someone in the sciences, but this is not mandatory.

Additional guidance for MD/PhD candidates: Letters of recommendation should be written by individuals who can evaluate your research potential as a physician-scientist. One letter should be from the research mentor with whom you have been most recently associated.
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: The Early Decision Program is available only for MD applicants (i.e. not for MD/PhD). The EDP Primary application deadline is August 1 and the Secondary application deadline is August 31.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: No relationship to the school is required for non-resident or international applicants.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: State residency is not required for non-residents of the United States.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: Accepted DACA status applicants are eligible to receive need-based financial aid from Yale School of Medicine.
medSchoolApplication.transferContact: transfers only permitted into second semester of the second year. Transfers are space dependent. See website below.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: YSM does not have a minimum GPA requirement for consideration.  All applications are reviewed holistically.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: YSM does not require a minimum number of credit hours in order to consider an applicant's postbacc or graduate coursework.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: U.S. Community College courses are acceptable.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Applicants can upload additional materials and letters at any time throughout the application cycle via the application portal.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
The admissions process is "need blind," which means that financial circumstances are not considered by the admissions committee when an application is evaluated. Financial aid is based on demonstrated financial need, and the full need of every accepted student (regardless of citizenship) will be met with a financial aid award. The goal of the financial aid program is to enable every accepted student to attend without unreasonable hardship. All financial aid applicants must submit the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) and the Yale School of Medicine financial aid application, which becomes available in January or February each year (online only). 

Detailed information about Yale School of Medicine financial aid can be found online:
https://medicine.yale.edu/md-program/financialaid/mdprogram/
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Tuition is set each year by the School of Medicine administration.

medSchoolPrograms.info: In collaboration with other schools at Yale University, the following joint degree programs are offered: MD/JD, MD/MHS, MD/MPH, MD/MBA and MD/MS in Personalized Medicine and Applied Engineering. Application to these joint degree programs occur post matriculation, typically during or after the second year of the MD program. Medical School advisers and advisers from the other Yale schools provide guidance for the application process and the period of enrollment.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: All accepted applicants choosing Yale School of Medicine must ‘commit’ or ‘plan’ to matriculate by this date. They must also immediately withdraw admission from all other schools. Applicants who ‘commit’ to matriculate also must immediately withdraw from waitlists at all other schools.
All applicants choosing Yale School of Medicine must ‘commit’ to enroll and immediately withdraw from waitlists at all other schools by this date.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
The minimum requirements for admission are:

1. Attendance for three academic years, or the equivalent, at an accredited college, university, or institute of technology.

2. Satisfactory completion of the following courses, including laboratory work:
- General Biology (2 semesters)
- General Chemistry (2 semesters)
- Organic Chemistry (1 semester)
- Biochemistry (1 semester - laboratory recommended, but not req.)
- General Physics (2 semesters)
- Biostatistics is recommended (not required) beginning in the 2026-27 application year.

Acceptable courses in these subjects are usually given 3-4 semester hours of academic credit per semester.

Pre-medical courses must be completed in a US, UK, or Canadian college/university. US Community College and online courses are acceptable, provided that the courses include laboratory work and are comparable in content to courses at four-year universities.  Please see https://medicine.yale.edu/md-program/admissions/requirements/ for more information.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The admissions process is holistic and contextual with no rigid "cut-offs". Grades, MCAT scores, medical and research experience, activities, personal qualities, letters of support, and interviews (if offered) are all considered. State of residence and citizenship are not factors. Interviews are selective and invitations to interview are extended after a complete review of application materials.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Shadowing of physicians is not required of applicants, but prospective students are encouraged to gain direct experience working or volunteering in healthcare settings.
